authority: $string rounds before it serializes. jsonata.org says only that a value is "converted to a JSON string using the JSON.stringify function", but that sentence names the three-parameter form whose replacer runs before ECMAScript's exact-number step — two of the same list's four casting bullets (functions to "", infinity/NaN throwing) are unreachable without a replacer — and jsonata.org's own published outputs are rounded ($sqrt(2) documented as 1.414213562373, byte-exact toPrecision(13), against an exact 1.4142135623730951). The digit COUNT is not documented and 15 is a recorded deviation: docs/spec.md 4.2.6 and jsntrs-jnv, decided 2026-08-15. jsonata.org, Other Operators, & (Concatenation): "If either or both of the operands are not strings, then they are first cast to string using the rules of the $string function", so the operator inherits the rule above rather than restating it. The inner & already cast the number, so $string sees a string and leaves it unchanged ("Strings are unchanged").
